title: Ramp Help Center
snippet:
To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.
Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses.
1. Open [Developer apps](https://app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer/apps) in Ramp.
2. For your first app, click **Start building**. If you already have an app, click **Create new app**.
3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types**, confirm **Client credentials** is turned on.
5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read`. If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

title: Introducing Ramp’s Technology Partner Program
snippet:
That’s why today we’re relaunching the Ramp Technology Partner Program: a clearer way to build with Ramp, refer customers to Ramp, and grow alongside Ramp. There are three ways in, real economics from the start, and a growing group of technology leaders already building with us.

Our recently refreshed API documentation makes it easier to understand what is available and get started. Partners can work with real-time spend data, approval workflows, user provisioning and spend controls, virtual cards, vendor payouts, and more.

That same belief also powers [Ramp Router](https://router.com/), our new early-access LLM router that launched last week: one API endpoint for accessing multiple AI models. Instead of wiring your app to one provider at a time, you send requests through our router which can choose the right model for the job based on quality, cost, and availability.

Not every partner needs an integration. Not every partner needs the same business model. The program is designed around three ways to work with Ramp.
### Referral: Make the introduction. Earn when customers choose Ramp.

Partnerships should get more valuable as the work compounds. The Ramp Technology Partner Program is designed to do that.
Partners are eligible to receive referral incentives and starts with access to the Partner Portal, aggregated client insights, a co-branded referral page, and Sandbox and Developer Console access. As partners grow, the program adds the support and investment needed to further build and go to market together.

title: docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/authorization.txt
snippet:
## Supported grant types
| Grant Type | Use Case | User Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Client Credentials** | Internal integrations, server-to-server | None required |
| **Authorization Code** | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required |
| **Refresh Token** | Renew access after an Authorization Code grant | None after the initial authorization |

`cards:read_vault` is available only to approved integrators; see [Virtual Cards](</developer-api/v1/virtual-cards#vault-api>). Scopes marked partners only appear in the partner Developer Console, not in a business's own Developer API settings. Some endpoints also require a Ramp plan feature and return `403` without it, even with the right scope.
## Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI
[Ramp MCP](</developer-api/v1/ramp-mcp>) and [Ramp CLI](</developer-api/v1/cli>) don't use OAuth scopes to limit access. A connection can do what the connecting user's Ramp role allows, so new tools don't fail with missing-scope errors.

title: How can I integrate Ramp Network with my platform or app?
snippet:
Once you've gathered the necessary materials for partnership, it's time to apply. Begin by completing [the form on our contact page,](https://rampnetwork.com/contact-sales) providing more insight into your company.
Following the initial application review (1-2 business days), you'll receive an email with the outcome – hopefully, an approval! This email should contain:
- Due diligence form
- Testing environment API key
- Guide on optimal Ramp Network widget implementation

Upon receiving compliance approval, we'll forward:
- **Your partnership contract draft**: Take the time to carefully review its contents, fill in the necessary details, and promptly return it to us.
- **Production API keys**: Your means to unlock full payment method access, enabling seamless interaction with various transaction options.
Subsequently, the official contract will be sent via **Docusign**. Your signature activates the full integration process.

*If you need any help, reach out to us at [partner@ramp.network](mailto:partner@ramp.network). We'll be more than happy to help you!*
